text: MS Monarch (formerly Monarch of the Seas) was the second of three Sovereign-class cruise ships owned by Royal Caribbean International. Built in 1991 at the Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyards in Saint-Nazaire, France, the ship was 73,941 GT and one of the largest cruise ships in the world at completion, capable of carrying up to 2,744 passengers. During her completion in 1990, about a third of the ship burned due to a welding equipment accident, with repair costs so high that it was uncertain if the vessel could be salvaged. After evaluation, the damaged bow section was removed, rebuilt, and the metal recycled to construct the next ship in the class, Majesty of the Seas. Monarch featured an outdoor basketball court, two shuffleboard courts, a rock climbing wall, and two full-sized saltwater pools; the rock-climbing wall was added during a 2003 refurbishment, and the fitness center, spa, and children's area were also enlarged. Prior to retirement from Royal Caribbean International, Monarch of the Seas sailed to the Bahamas from Port Canaveral, Florida. In 2007, she became the first major cruise ship to be captained by a woman, Swede Karin Stahre-Janson, who remained the only female captain until 2010 when Sarah Breton took command of MS Artemis of P&O Cruises. On April 1, 2013, after 22 years of service with Royal Caribbean International, Monarch was transferred to Spain's Pullmantur Cruises, joining her sister ship MS Sovereign. Before sailing under Pullmantur, she underwent a refurbishment of cabins, casino, and shops. She began year-round sailing in the Southern Caribbean on April 27, 2013. In 2020, amid the COVID-19 pandemic, Monarch and MS Sovereign were placed into "cold lay-up," and Pullmantur filed for financial reorganization. The interiors of both ships were stripped of all valuable items. Pullmantur announced that MS Monarch, MS Sovereign, and MS Horizon would be sold to breakers in Aliağa, Turkey. Monarch was beached on July 22, 2020, and scrapping began on April 5, 2021, starting with the removal of the pilot's cabinet. On December 15, 1998, after evacuating a sick passenger in Philipsburg, Sint Maarten, Monarch of the Seas grazed a reef while departing, opening a 40 by 2-meter gash along the starboard hull. The ship began taking on water and sank by the bow, with three watertight compartments fully flooded and several others partially flooded. It was intentionally grounded on a sandbar to prevent further sinking, and all passengers were evacuated safely with no deaths. The grounding breached two diesel fuel tanks and an overflow tank, resulting in a small fuel spill of approximately 100 US gallons (380 L; 83 imp gal). A joint investigation by the Norwegian Maritime Investigator and the United States Coast Guard concluded the accident resulted from "a myriad of human performance deficiencies," including navigation done visually without electronic aids and failure to update charts after a vital buoy was relocated. The ship was drydocked for three months at Atlantic Marine's Mobile, Alabama, where 114 compartments were cleaned, machinery was replaced, 460 tons of shell plating and 18 miles (29 km) of electrical wiring were replaced. American comedian John Pinette referenced the incident in his 2005 DVD 'I Say Nay Nay'. In August 2005, while docked at the Port of Los Angeles, a sewage pipe maintenance incident released a small amount of raw sewage and an unknown amount of hydrogen sulfide gas, killing three crew members and injuring 19 others; the deaths were nearly instantaneous because the crew was not wearing breathing apparatus. On January 30, 2006, 38-year-old Captain Joern Rene Klausen was found dead in his stateroom aboard Monarch, returning from a three-night cruise to Ensenada, Mexico; the death was reported to be from natural causes. On March 14, 2020, Panama repatriated 1,504 Colombian tourists from Monarch due to coronavirus fears, as the port of Cartagena, Colombia was closed, requiring them to fly from Colón, Panama. On April 17, 2020, a Honduran crew member died of the virus in a hospital in Panama City after being medically evacuated for breathing difficulties and testing positive.
